text:
sara: Heads-up — before we flip tenant routing for active-active writes, we should agree on a probe-driven, staggered cutover. want to avoid any accidental residency violations during ramp.

amit: +1. Can you sketch the probe -> weight ramp rules? worried about transient latency spikes causing premature traffic shifts.

sara: idea: keep primary steering weight on resident region until probe success window of 5m. probes check latency, 2xx rate, and consent header presence. if probes healthy, ramp weights 10% every 2m up to target; if probes fail, rollback to 100% resident immediately.

marco: so a combination of canary + progressive steering. Are probes per-tenant or per-region? per-tenant seems expensive.

sara: per-tenant for high-risk tenants (legal/regulatory), otherwise per-region aggregated with sampled tenants. We'll tag tenants with residency_level: high/medium/low.

linda: what about in-flight requests? switching weights mid-flight might route next token to other region and cause KV cache mismatch.

amit: good catch. runtime needs to pin request session_id -> route for the lifetime of the operation. only new sessions observe updated weights. add TTL for session pinning e.g., 30s.

marco: also need a safety net for eventual consistency: when we route to non-resident region for a write, attach a transient header `x-residency-proxy: true` so downstream can decide sync vs async mode.

sara: agreed. propose this minimal config snippet for the routing policy:

```
{"probe_window_s":300,
 "ramp_step_pct":10,
 "ramp_interval_s":120,
 "session_pin_ttl_s":30,
 "consent_header":"x-customer-consent",
 "fallback":"resident-only"}
```

linda: how do we detect consent_header? some mobile clients strip custom headers. we need server-side enforcement or token claim.

amit: token claim is safer. add `residency_consent` claim on service tokens; probes validate either header or claim. fallback if neither present.

sara: telemetry: emit `probe_result` with dims [region, tenant, probe_type, ok|fail], and `ramp_event` with new_weight. we'll add an alert if >2 consecutive probe failures in 10m.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: routing-probe-service v1.3.2 -> staging in 2m :hourglass_flowing_sand:

marco: runbook notes: if rollback occurs, automation should set weights back to resident and open P0 with oncall. manual override must live in console (no CLI-only ops).

linda: ops checklist for canary: 1) enable tenant tags, 2) verify token claims for sample tenants, 3) smoke writes from region B to confirm header tagging, 4) watch probe_result dashboard.

sara: timeline: staging run today, small canary (10 tenants) tomorrow, full ramp next week if green. i'll add the stagger config to the RFC follow-up doc and link it.

amit: perfect. also please add an integration test that simulates a spike (latency 3x) during a ramp and asserts rollback triggers within 60s.

sara: noted — i'll create the ticket and tag @marco for the integration test. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
